handoff.purpose: Render tier-2, gate, and combined reports as text.

symbols.name: render_tier2
symbols.note: Formats tier-2 LLM task-success results, including skipped, per-task rows, aggregate, truncation warning, and errored tasks.

symbols.name: render_gate
symbols.note: Formats the advisory gate report: pass/fail, regressions, improved, new, missing, errored primary/quarantine, focus-withheld, and baseline-update hint.

symbols.name: render
symbols.note: Concatenates tier-1, arms, and tier-2 renderings.

claims.text: This never blocks anything by itself; it is a local developer command.
claims.why: render_gate only builds a string; there is no blocking, no side effect, and no call to any gating or mutation API in this chunk.

claims.text: TOK_B is what was actually sent to the model (may be truncated to fit the context window); TOK_B(true) is the real, untruncated whole-repo size.
claims.why: The code prints tokens_B as 'TOK_B' and tokens_B_true (fallback tokens_B) as 'TOK_B(true)', and the truncation warning says B (sent) understates the real baseline when truncated.

claims.text: B (sent) above understates the real whole-repo baseline; a truncated baseline is a WEAKER one, not a fair comparison.
claims.why: The warning is emitted only when result['b_truncated_any'] is truthy, and the text matches the claim.

claims.text: SKIPPED (not counted in the aggregate above)
claims.why: The errored tasks are listed separately after the aggregate line, and the aggregate uses only success_A and success_B counts from the result dict, not from errored.

claims.text: This FAILS the gate (a broken primary corpus must scream)
claims.why: The text says errored primary tasks fail the gate; the code does not alter it, and the final 'No primary-tier task lost recall' line is suppressed when errored_primary is non-empty.

claims.text: reported only, does NOT fail the gate
claims.why: The block is separate and does not influence the pass/fail banner or the final no-regression line.

claims.text: NOT a recall regression, reported only
claims.why: Focus-withheld entries are rendered in their own block and are not added to the REGRESSIONS list.

claims.text: Run 'python -m daedalus.eval --update-baseline' to intentionally accept the current numbers as the new baseline (explicit only, never automatic).
claims.why: The command's behavior (that it updates the baseline and is never automatic) lives in the CLI/harness, not in this rendering chunk.

claims.text: A ~= B success at a fraction of B's tokens
claims.why: This is a claim about the meaning of the result dict's success_A/success_B/tokens values; the comparison itself is not computed or validated here.

claims.text: ADVISORY regression-ratchet report -- see harness.run_gate docstring.
claims.why: The harness.run_gate docstring is in another module; this chunk cannot verify its contents.

claims.text: Errored tasks (result.get: absent for any hand-built pre-existing gate result dict, and always absent -> no lines added when there are none).
claims.why: The code uses result.get('errored_primary') and result.get('errored_quarantine') with a default of [], so absent keys produce no lines.

claims.text: Focus-withheld tasks (result.get: absent for any hand-built pre-existing gate result dict)
claims.why: The code uses result.get('focus_withheld') with a default of [].

claims.text: a fence fail-closing on a task's own focus file is NOT a recall regression (see harness.run_gate)
claims.why: The claim about the fence and harness.run_gate's behavior is outside this rendering function.

observations.what: render_gate checks 'regressions' and 'errored_primary' with direct subscripting (result['regressions'], result['errored_primary']) but uses .get for errored_quarantine and focus_withheld; a hand-built gate dict missing 'regressions' or 'errored_primary' would raise KeyError before the .get fallbacks matter.

render_tier2 divides tok_a by tok_b with a guard for tok_b being falsy, but the same guard is not used for the aggregate ratio line; if tok_b is 0, the f-string '100 * tok_a / tok_b' raises ZeroDivisionError.
The comment says 'a check that CANNOT FAIL' is requested, but no such check exists in this chunk; the code has no assertions or self-referential fixtures.
The comment says 'a refusal with NO REACHABLE REPAIR' is requested, but this chunk only renders strings; no refusal or repair path exists here.
The comment says 'a rule INVERTED with respect to its own stated goal' is requested, but no rule enforcement exists in this chunk; it only formats output.
The comment says 'a value parsed from output whose FORMAT IS NOT PINNED' is requested, but this chunk does not parse any output; it only formats result dicts.

risks: render_gate | medium | Direct subscript of result['regressions'] and result['errored_primary'] will KeyError on a hand-built gate dict missing those keys, despite the .get fallbacks for other fields. | Test render_gate with a dict lacking 'regressions' and 'errored_primary' and observe the exception.
